audience.programmeDescription: Leiden International Studies investigates global developments through culture, history, politics and economics. Students specialise in one world region and learn a language associated with it, then apply their knowledge through research and an international consultancy project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The three UCR compositions offer substantial international politics and political economy, cultural and historical inquiry, or conflict and global justice. They integrate subject study with research methods, but do not reproduce Leiden’s cumulative Arabic-language training, systematic Africa-area sequence or compulsory area thesis. Stylistics and community rhetoric contribute to the study of meaning and persuasion but do not reproduce the sociolinguistics and intercultural-analysis courses.

curriculum.limitation: The illustrated pathway contains 60 EC in each year, including 30 EC of open choice in year three. Africa and Arabic follow the official ordering of the available areas and languages. The research-method and thematic-seminar choices, and thesis seminar, are allocated through preference surveys subject to capacity. Arabic 2 requires Arabic 1; Arabic 3 requires both earlier courses. Language and Culture in Practice requires Arabic 1 and 2, with Arabic 3 passed or taken alongside it. PRINS requires 100 curricular EC. The 15-EC thesis requires a passed 10-EC Thematic Seminar and 100 EC from years one and two. It is a 10,000-word research paper, supported by required seminar participation, a proposal, literature review and draft. The ordinary first-year study-advice threshold is 45 EC and a passed first foreign-language course. Open choice can include a minor, exchange or internship under the applicable approval rules.

componentNotes.curr-component-21: 30 EC of genuine open choice; no specific minor, internship or exchange is assumed.
componentNotes.curr-5183vpra9y: 10-EC collaborative consultancy project with individual and team assessment; entry requires 100 curricular EC.
componentNotes.curr-5183v5t12y: 15-EC individual thesis within a compulsory area seminar, subject to entry and submission requirements.
